description:
Facing off against his brother Sylvain of the Hartford Whalers, Pierre Turgeon netted his first career NHL goal on a Buffalo power play to open the scoring. He added another later in the game, marking the first two of his 515 career goals. Just one year after his rookie season, Turgeon led the Sabres in scoring—all while still in his teens.

description:
In his NHL debut, Sergei Fedorov immediately thrilled Detroit Red Wings fans by scoring his first career goal. During a power play on the road in New Jersey, Fedorov executed a beautiful give-and-go with Steve Yzerman before firing the puck into the back of the net. His goal was part of an impressive rookie campaign in which he registered 31 goals and 79 points. The former Hart Trophy and two-time Selke Trophy winner spent the first 13 of his 18 seasons with Detroit, where he won three Stanley Cup championships.

description:
Positioned at the side of the net, Patrice Bergeron buries the game-tying goal on a late Boston power play — his first career NHL goal — with just minutes to go in the third period. It was the first of many clutch moments for Bergeron, who went on to spend his entire 19-season career in Boston, winning the Selke Trophy a record six times along the way.

description:
Henrik Lundqvist, the New York Rangers’ all-time leader in career wins, enjoyed a remarkable 15-season run—every game played in a Blueshirt. A late steal in the seventh round of the draft, Lundqvist rose to greatness and earned his place in the Hockey Hall of Fame. He picked up his first NHL win by outdueling Martin Brodeur and never looked back, finishing his rookie season with stellar numbers: a .922 save percentage, 2.24 goals-against average, and a 30-12-9 record.

description:
Hartford’s first round selection in the 1981 NHL Draft (4th overall), Ron Francis went on to an incredible NHL career that spanned 23 seasons in which parts of 16 of them were spent with the Hartford Whalers/Carolina Hurricanes franchise.  The franchise’s all-time points leader, Francis scored his first career NHL goal during a Whalers’ power play facing the Toronto Maple Leafs in just his second NHL game.  After a clean faceoff win, Mark Howe unleashed a one-timer from the point, and the rebound found Francis crashing the net—where he buried it.  The Hall of Famer completed his rookie season with an impressive 68 points in 59 games.

description:
The 1993-94 Calder Trophy winner, Martin Brodeur made his NHL debut two seasons prior, on March 26, 1992, earning his first career win. In a sharp 24-save performance that included several point-blank stops, Brodeur offered an early glimpse of the brilliance that would define his Hall of Fame career. It was the first of a record-setting 691 wins—an NHL mark that may stand untouched for generations.
